questions.knowledge_point: Writing a Complex Number in Exponential Form
questions.problem: Write the complex number $z=-1+\text{i}$ in exponential form.
questions.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the second quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-1)| \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{3\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

questions.problem: Write the complex number $z=-2+2\sqrt{3}\,\text{i}$ in exponential form.
questions.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{(2\sqrt{3})}^{2}} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the second quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2})| \\  & =\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})| \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{2\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=4$ and $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=4\,{\text{e}}^{2\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$

questions.problem: Write the complex number $z=3-2\text{i}$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ giving $\theta $ in radians to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
To write $z$ in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-2}{3})| \\  & =2\pi -|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\frac{2}{3})| \\  & ≈5.695.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=\sqrt{13}$ and $\theta =5.695$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=\sqrt{13}\,{\text{e}}^{5.695\,\text{i}}.
$$

$$

$$

$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{7\pi \text{i}/4}.

questions.problem: Write the complex number $z=\sqrt{3}+3\text{i}$ in exponential form.
questions.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z=r{\text{e}}^{\text{i}\theta },$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z),$ we first calculate $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=2\sqrt{3}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get

$$
z=2\sqrt{3}\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/3}.
$$

$$

Now, since $z$ lies in the first quadrant, we can find the angle $\theta $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=3\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}$ into $z=r{e}^{\text{i}\theta },$ we get 

$$
z=3\sqrt{2}\,{\text{e}}^{\pi \text{i}/4}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Write the complex number $z=4+4\textrm{i}$ in exponential form.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To write our complex number in the form $z = r\textrm{e}^{\textrm{i}\theta},$ where $r=|z|$ and $\theta = \arg(z),$ we first calculate $r\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}r=|z| & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $z$ lies in the first quadrant of the complex plane, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta =\operatorname{arg}⁡(z) & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x}) \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $r=4\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ into $z=re^{\textrm{i}\theta},$ we get

$$
z = 4\sqrt{2}\,\textrm{e}^{\pi\textrm{i}/4}.
$$
